messages.subject: hierarchical binomial simulation: JAGS vs. Stan
parts:
Sorry -- last message fat fingered out of my mailer before
I could format and attach code.


I've attached:

-- Stan model (basic parameterization)

-- JAGS model (matching parameterization)

-- fake data simulator and fitter

-- print output from both fits

The models are basically Adam Selz's with a bit of reformatting.

Here are the results:

JAGS Stan


time 30s 30s(*)

n_eff(**)
u0 180 4000
bx 90 4000
sigma 290 4000

R-hat(***)
max (hier) 1.04 1.000
max (low) 2.00 1.000

---------------------

(*) Stan time does not include model compilation.

(**) n_eff calculated using R2jags for JAGS and
RStan for Stan; Stan's should be more conservative

(***) R-hat calculated using R2jags for JAGS and
RStan for Stan; numbers are maximum R-hat for
the hierarchical parameters and maximum R-hat for
lower-level parameters.

Both systems estimated posterior means that matched the
simulated values well.

Stan's drawing effectively independently samples in each
iteration, at least according to RStan's n_eff calculations.
Stan converges in fewer than 50 iterations, so using 1000
warmup iterations is cutting n_eff/s in half or so.

I ran a few times and the pattern was consistent.

Adam -- would you mind sending me your data so I
can try that? The above is with data simulated from
the model.

JAGS is version 3.3.0.
Stan is RStan 1.3.0.
R is 3.0.0 GUI 64-bit.
Hardware is the latest Macbook Pro.

- Bob
